why: Overwrite path: the tool snapshots only when the file exists and append is false (file_write.py:125), SafetyStore.snapshot copies the previous bytes to snapshots/<id>/original and appends one entry (journal.py:81-97), and undo restores then appends the marker (journal.py:169-178). Executed: `uv run --quiet pytest tests/safety/test_journal.py tests/unit/test_file_write_snapshot.py tests/unit/test_cli_undo.py tests/config/test_safety.py -q` -> 39 passed; canonical `pytest tests/config tests/safety tests/unit tests/learning tests/memory tests/eval tests/validation -q` -> 1463 passed, 28 skipped. Supplied live measurement (coordinator, not re-run by me): v1->v2 leaves exactly one entry, snapshot bytes v1, target v2, `cortex undo last` -> v1. The restore is byte-for-byte, but not metadata-for-metadata: a 0755 file came back 0600 in my probe (see STD-4). Same-user path only; the compose/host split is the STD-4 fatal.

quote: if not append and file_path.exists() and self._store is not None:
why: New-file path: `file_path.exists()` is false, so no snapshot is taken and no journal line is appended; `append=True` is excluded by the same condition. Tests: tests/unit/test_file_write_snapshot.py::TestNonDestructiveWrites::test_new_file_creates_no_snapshot_or_journal_entry asserts no journal file, an empty snapshots dir and no snapshot_id metadata; test_append_is_not_snapshotted asserts v1v2 and no entry. My run of the four feature files: 39 passed. Supplied live measurement: writing a new file created no journal entry. No finding.

`_select('last')` walks the journal backwards, skipping undo markers and ids already in the `undone` set (journal.py:202-208), so consecutive undos revert consecutive overwrites; `undo <id>` refuses an already-undone id (journal.py:148-149). Tests: test_two_overwrites_undo_in_reverse_order (v2 then v1; actions ['file_write','file_write','undo','undo']) and test_two_undo_last_calls_revert_two_overwrites_in_reverse_order; 39 passed in my run. Supplied live measurement: v1->v2->v3 produced two entries and two undos returned v2 then v1, ending at 4 journal lines. No finding.

The default store is `~/.local/share/cortex`, outside the repo; tests/config/test_safety.py::TestDefaults::test_default_store_is_outside_the_repository asserts `not safety.store_dir.resolve().is_relative_to(repo_root)`. I ran `git status --porcelain` at the commit and the tree is clean (no store files), matching the supplied live check. Residual advisory: `SAFETY_STORE_DIR` is unconstrained, so an operator can point the store inside the repo and no runtime guard rejects it; the test pins only the default. The spec's 'never' is currently a default, not an enforced invariant.

The tool checks the snapshot before writing and returns success=False on UndoError without opening the file (file_write.py:125-135); SafetyStore.snapshot converts copy and journal failures to UndoError and removes the half-written snapshot directory (journal.py:78-100). Tests: test_snapshot_failure_refuses_the_overwrite (monkeypatched store raises UndoError; target stays v1, no entry), test_directory_target_is_refused (a real shutil.copy2 failure on a directory), test_a_directory_target_fails_the_copy, test_copy_failure_removes_the_snapshot_dir_and_raises; 39 passed. Supplied measurement: snapshot failure was exercised with a fake/store error and a directory target, not a real read-only filesystem. Residual: store construction is eager at startup, so an unwritable store aborts the app before any write and even with snapshots disabled (my measurement; see STD-3). The AC's write-refusal path itself is met.

`@cli.command('undo')` defines `target: str = typer.Argument('last')` (so `cortex undo` == `cortex undo last`), has no confirmation, prints `error: ...` to stderr and raises `typer.Exit(1)` on UndoError, and prints `restored: ...`/`snapshot: ...` on success (cli.py:413-435). Tests: tests/unit/test_cli_undo.py covers last, id, two reverse calls, stderr+exit 1, already undone and unknown id (6 cases; all pass in my 39-test run). The no-snapshot recipe is tested at the store level (test_entry_without_a_snapshot_prints_the_recipe asserts the recipe is in the UndoError string, which the CLI prefixes with `error:`); there is no CLI-level test of that exact entry. Same-user path only; the compose PermissionError is STD-4 and the LLM_API_KEY prerequisite is STD-5.

Most of the contract holds: the action line has exactly id, ts, action, targets, snapshot, undo_recipe, status (journal.py:87-95); the undo marker has id, ts, action='undo', target_id, targets, status='undone' (171-178); the journal is opened O_APPEND and never rewritten (240-244); undo derives `undone` by scanning markers, and test_undo_last_restores_bytes_and_appends_an_undone_marker asserts the original line's status stays 'applied' after undo (test_journal.py:155-158); 39 tests pass. Finding (actionable, advisory): the entry is appended inside snapshot() before the caller's write (the write is file_write.py:140). Measured with a 0444 target: the tool returned 'Permission denied', the journal held one ('file_write','applied') line, and the target was still v1. The line claims an action that did not happen; `undo last` then restores v1 over v1 and appends a marker, consuming a step. No test covers a post-snapshot write failure. Fix: append an `aborted`/`failed` marker on the write error and have undo skip it, or journal `status: intent` and mark applied after the write, keeping the snapshot for crash safety. Residual: a single os.write with O_APPEND is atomic on a local filesystem, but there is no cross-process test (supplied: concurrency not stress-tested) and a torn line is silently skipped by entries(), which can drop the newest entry.

Wiring is correct: initialize_app passes `safety=settings.safety` to register_meta_tools, which forwards it through get_meta_tools to FileWriteTool(safety) (meta/__init__.py:40, 66), so the app's file_write gets the store; the eval sandbox constructs `FileWriteTool()` with no settings (src/cortex/eval/sandbox.py:141), so it is unaffected; `FileWriteTool()` alone still writes without a store (test_without_settings_there_is_no_store). Coverage advisory (B3): no test calls `register_meta_tools(..., safety=...)`, `get_meta_tools(safety)` or `initialize_app`; grep finds only `register_meta_tools(registry)` in tests/unit/test_tools_meta.py. The wiring is a one-line change but is not exercised through the real entry point; the supplied live check names the tool and store, not main.py/initialize_app. The eager SafetyStore construction at startup is the STD-3 finding.

Conventions held: the field defaults to True, is documented in config.yaml:76, .env.example:43 and docs/specs/safety-net.md:84/157, and the SAFETY_ prefix is registered in tests/settings_env.py:29 so the CFG4 ambient-env guard scrubs it; tests/config/test_safety.py covers default, env, YAML and the composed root; 39 passed. Findings (actionable, advisory): (1) `SAFETY_SNAPSHOT_ENABLED=false` still creates the store: FileWriteTool(safety) constructs SafetyStore (file_write.py:21) and __init__ mkdirs snapshots/ (journal.py:56,59); I measured store/ and store/snapshots/ existing with no journal. (2) With an unwritable parent I measured `get_meta_tools(safety)` raising PermissionError for enabled=True and enabled=False, and initialize_app does not catch it (main.py:221), so an unwritable store aborts startup even though the documented policy is to refuse the overwrite and even with the escape hatch. Fix: make _ensure_snapshots_dir best-effort/log (the write-time snapshot already fails closed) and construct the store lazily or only for the registered tool. (3) Docs drift: ADR-0021 line 5 still says '#147/#148 designed' while this commit marks slice 2 implemented, and CONTEXT.md has no backup/snapshot/journal/undo entries although the spec names it as the vocabulary source and docs/agents/domain.md:12 makes CONTEXT.md canonical for vocabulary.

The same-user modes are correct: snapshots dir 0700, snapshot dir 0700, snapshot file 0600, journal 0600 (tests/safety/test_journal.py::test_store_files_are_private; supplied live modes 0700/0600/0600), and undo refuses a snapshot outside snapshots/ (journal.py:164). Fatal integration breach: when file_write is enabled (TOOLS_ALLOW includes it; the default allow-list is read-only), the documented deployment pairs a root compose app (docker-compose.yml:47 'The app container still runs as root ... non-root is #120'; no USER in the Dockerfile) with a host CLI, and SafetyStore creates the journal and per-entry snapshot dirs/files as the process user with no chown to the store owner. BackupService has exactly that chown for dumps (#146: backup.py:354 and _chown_to_store_owner at 359-370, whose docstring states that a root container writes root-owned files while the host CLI needs the store user's ownership), but SafetyStore has none. I simulated the cross-user store: a root busybox in a host bind mount wrote journal.jsonl 0600 root:root and snapshots/abc123/original 0600 root:root inside a 0700 root dir; as uid 1000 `cat journal.jsonl` -> Permission denied, `Path(...).is_file()` -> PermissionError, and `SafetyStore.undo('last')` -> PermissionError, not UndoError, so cli.py:430 does not catch it (traceback/exit 1 instead of the recipe). Even after a chown, the journal stores writer-side absolute paths (`snapshot` is /var/lib/cortex/safety/... in compose, `targets` is /app/...), while the host CLI's store is ~/.local/share/cortex and the host has no mapping for the app's /app, so the host undo cannot find the snapshot or the target; the shared store is portable only if the snapshot path is store-relative and the target namespace is resolved, or undo runs in the same namespace (the docs do not say). Secondary (advisory, measured): restore loses the original mode - a 0755 file came back 0600 because the snapshot copy is chmodded to 0600 and _restore copystat's it back (journal.py:229), while the docstring claims 'preserving its stats' (217). Also `targets[0]` is used unconfined (162), so a hand-edited journal can write any path (same-user threat model, #120 boundary). Fix: chown new artifacts to the store uid/gid like backups, persist the original mode in the entry, store the snapshot path relative to the store, and document/handle the target namespace.

CLI shape passes: typer command, `last` default, no prompt, error to stderr with Exit(1), restored/snapshot output (cli.py:413-435); the 6 CLI tests pass in my 39-test run. Findings (actionable, advisory): (1) `settings = get_settings()` loads the composed root; LLMSettings.api_key is required (src/cortex/config/models.py:57), so from an empty cwd with LLM_API_KEY unset `cortex undo` exits 1 with an uncaught pydantic ValidationError instead of the journal/UndoError path (I reproduced it with CliRunner: exit 1, empty stdout, exception 'api_key Field required'). This repeats the unrelated-secret prerequisite the #146 review flagged for backup:create/restore, unfixed for the recovery command. Build SafetySettings directly (or accept --store-dir) and report a clean `error:`. (2) When every entry is undone, a further `undo last` raises UndoError('journal is empty') (journal.py:209) although the journal is not empty; I measured it. (3) The no-snapshot recipe path has no CLI-level test (store-level only).
